narration: Welcome to the Miniature Paintings gallery. This piece, accession number NM 69.2/5, is a striking example of the Mewar school from around 1650 CE, painted in opaque watercolour on paper and measuring 24 by 34 centimeters. It depicts the dramatic moment from the Ramayana when Lakshmana disfigures the demoness Surpanakha after her disguise is exposed, set against the flat red background typical of Mewar works. These paintings were produced in the workshops of Udaipur, commissioned by the local rulers, and they helped bring the epic to life in vivid, bold colours. Enjoy exploring this fascinating glimpse into 17th‑century Indian art.
